prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose Your Pet Companion Journey", "I'll guide you through choosing your new companion path!"]
1: ["Signing into your existing account automatically restores all previously created pets and companion data."]
2: ["Select Companion Demeanor and Personality"]
3: ["Verifying desktop overlay compatibility and spawning pet graphics..."]
4: ["Mastering Your Desktop Companion", "Quickly learn how to position, chat with, or hide your companion anytime.", "Right-click pet for quick menu; Drag to place anywhere; Double-click to chat"]
5: ["Select Your Setup Speed", "Choose Instant Adoption to launch in 30 seconds or Custom Pet to design from scratch.", "Continue Setup"]
6: ["Bonus Starter Accessory Pack Unlocked!"]
7: ["Choose Fast Guest Start or Sync Account to Save Pet Progress"]
8: ["Play Chime When Desktop Ready"]
9: ["Tip: You can hide or summon your pet anytime from the system tray menu or by pressing Ctrl+Shift+P."]

verdicts.problem: mentions bonuses or free extra items
suggests skipping or getting around required sign-in step
